components.title: France's 2010 reform: change in each status at 60 (points)¹

items.label: Standard error of the employment change

components.text: A later pension is not later work: in France, the Netherlands and Austria most of the difference went to unemployment, disability and sick leave. This is the ground for H2

footnote:
Rabaté and Rochut (2020), Journal of Pension Economics and Finance 19(3), tables 4 and 5
Worked out: 20.9 ÷ 47.8
notes: Where do people go when their pension is delayed? France's 2010 reform raised the minimum claiming age from 60 to 61. Rabaté and Rochut use a one-in-twenty administrative sample from the pension fund and compare adjacent birth cohorts. At age 60, retirement falls by 47.8 points, and only 20.9 of those points go into employment. Unemployment rises 13.4, inactivity 6.2, disability 5.9 and sickness 1.4, and the five add up to exactly 47.8. The Netherlands looks the same: one month past the old pension age, employment is up 21.2 points and disability 12.7. In Austria unemployment rose 12.5 points for men and 11.8 for women. China has a ready channel too: Article 7 of the Measures extends unemployment benefit up to the statutory retirement age for claimants within a year of it. So my outcomes cannot stop at employment. Unemployment and pension claiming must be measured separately, and that is hypothesis H2.
